limits: All timings are local guest workloads, not gdev frame measurements. Paired controls include setup and complete decoded output; timing equality and numerical checks are outside the clock.
Point-grid output includes all heads and point rows; set output includes all keys. The relationship workload includes construction, removal and the retained prior bucket.

Sparse indices measure one live bit per 32 slots and do not fetch component values. Dense indices have all bits set. ECS batch cases include initial world construction; payload-only and membership-transition cases are separate.

Dense ECS batches use a direct rebuild to avoid the measured regression from the first incremental implementation. Structural sparse changes still copy the flat mask array once. The page prototype is not integrated: a read-view design would be needed to avoid per-word tree walks.
Physics compares complete state/contact outputs for 56 existing and 12 new multi-walker scenarios against exact old source overlays, and measures normal and prepared physics separately.
The queue pair compares current individual versus batch submissions with the compiler workaround, not old versus new compiler timings. Traces are disabled.

Compiler and standard-library paths belong to the user; neither sibling checkout was changed. The isolated reduction still fails under the current compiler until Blot fixes generic array layout inference.
The catalog retains long numerical witnesses as length, SHA-256 of compact JSON, first and last eight words. Full arrays were independently checked and are retained in the local cache.
Committed guest memory is capacity, not live allocation volume or host process peak. Paired overlay guests are reused across cases; per-workload catalog capacities have separate guests.
Host activity caused timing variation; an isolated dense-physics repeat and the earlier preliminary run are retained alongside the final samples.
languageRecommendations: Preserve the instantiated nominal record layout through generic array generation and return; reject ambiguous layouts instead of emitting corrupted data.
Improve uniqueness analysis for freshly generated nominal-record arrays edited in a loop, using the point-grid reduction from the previous collection review.
Recognize scalar population-count and trailing-zero idioms and preserve in-place array reuse across safe dense/sparse control flow.
reproduce: Use the compiler and standard library hashes recorded above.
